reason: The text explicitly identifies Yahweh (יְהוָה) as 'the God of your fathers' and 'the God of the children of Israel.' God refers to Israel as 'my people' (עַמִּי) and instructs that they 'shall serve God' (תַּעַבְדוּן אֶת־הָאֱלֹהִים) on the mountain. The passage establishes a divine covenant relationship wherein the Hebrews/Israelites are clearly presented as the people and worshippers of Yahweh, which constitutes portrayal as followers of this God.
